## 固定收益市場主線

美國就業增長強勁，薪資月增幅也加快，強化市場對聯準會12月再度升息的預期，美國公債因而回吐部分一週漲幅。賣壓集中在短天期：2年期殖利率上升4.92個基點至4.5115%，10年期上升2.27個基點至4.8574%。非農就業報告挑戰了經濟正在放緩的預期，但本週公債的大部分漲幅仍得以保留，投資人持續評估科技股估值下修，以及人工智慧投資前景轉趨不明的影響。

10月非農就業增加16.5萬人，前期數字大幅上修，整體失業率降至4.1%。舊金山聯準銀行總裁Mary Daly表示，穩健的勞動市場讓決策官員有空間處理頑固通膨。不過，對難以找到足夠工作的人而言，處境並不輕鬆：涵蓋範圍更廣的勞動力低度運用指標上升，非自願兼職人數增加，失業期間也拉長。

風險偏好的回升並不全面。半導體類股反彈4.21%，美國投資級與高收益債利差大致持平。軟銀債券在亞洲交易時段走弱，歐洲公司債則較有支撐，近期科技業新債提供的優厚條件帶動其表現。AI融資之外，Braskem重整協商惡化，Brightspeed則尋求最高$30億的新資金。整體市場雖然回穩，這些借款人各自的融資問題仍不容忽視。

## 強勁就業抑制美國公債漲勢

週五公布就業數據前，市場原本已布局期待公債進一步上漲。就業報告打斷這波行情。Bloomberg盤中報導顯示，2年期美國公債殖利率一度上升9個基點至4.55%，隨後回落至約4.51%。最初的賣壓隨交易進行而消退，較持久的調整集中在對未來幾次聯準會決策敏感的天期。

收盤時，各天期殖利率均上升，曲線趨平。5年期上升4.04個基點至4.6449%，30年期上升1.06個基點至5.2645%；2年與10年期利差收窄2.65個基點至34.59個基點，2年與30年期利差縮減3.86個基點至75.3個基點。長端回吐幅度較小，10年期殖利率一週仍下降7.15個基點，一個月下降42.41個基點。2年期一週下降7.61個基點，30年期則下降4.37個基點。

週五10年期殖利率的升幅主要來自實質殖利率：同天期抗通膨公債殖利率上升1.5個基點至2.6127%，通膨補償上升0.77個基點至2.2447%。但拉長至一週，實質殖利率上升2.82個基點，損益兩平通膨率下降9.97個基點。即使週五就業消息較強，一週名目公債的漲勢仍由通膨補償下降支撐。一個月來，實質殖利率下降29.91個基點，損益兩平通膨率下降12.5個基點。

就業改善不只反映在單一總數。美國勞工統計局將8月就業增幅由13.3萬人上修至18.6萬人，9月由2.9萬人上修至6萬人，合計比原先估計多8.4萬人。10月增加16.5萬人，相較前12個月平均每月增加4.8萬人，公布前的市場共識為6.5萬人。民間就業增加15.9萬人，高於預期的6.4萬人及9月修正後的7.8萬人；政府就業則在9月修正後減少1.8萬人之後，增加6,000人。

專業與商業服務業增加7萬人，高於過去一年平均每月的1.5萬人，其中技術服務增加3.3萬人、行政服務2.8萬人、管理業9,000人。醫療保健增加4.2萬人，高於前一年平均的3.1萬人，包括醫院增加1.6萬人、居家醫療增加1.1萬人。運輸與倉儲增加2.5萬人，主要來自快遞業增加1.7萬人及航空運輸增加4,000人。

製造業增加1.9萬人，高於市場共識的5,000人及9月修正後的1.3萬人。電子業貢獻7,000人，機械與初級金屬業各增加4,000人。Bloomberg報導，電腦與電子產品製造業就業增幅創四年來最大。非住宅營建持續增聘，但住宅建築就業減少拖累整體營建業。先前隨AI快速普及而流失就業的資訊與金融活動業，則初步出現趨穩跡象。

薪資月增幅高於預期，年增率則仍低於近年的一般水準。平均時薪增加$0.14、月增0.4%，至$38.00，高於市場預期的0.3%；年增3.1%，高於預期的2.9%，但低於9月修正後的3.2%。生產及非管理職員工時薪也上升0.4%、增加$0.12，至$32.75。平均每週工時維持34.4小時，製造業維持40.5小時，加班時數小幅升至3.1小時；生產及非管理職員工每週工時則減少0.1小時至33.8小時。

家戶調查同時呈現勞動參與增加與勞動力運用不足加劇。U-3整體失業率由4.2%降至4.1%，市場原先預期持平；勞動參與率由61.8%升至61.9%，就業人口比率由59.2%升至59.3%。但涵蓋範圍更廣的U-6勞動力低度運用率由7.6%升至7.9%，因經濟因素從事兼職的人數增加33.9萬人至484萬人。失業期間中位數達11.9週，為2021年以來最長。招聘轉強之際，部分勞工要取得全職工作或重返職場，反而面臨更大困難。

聯準會利率定價小幅朝進一步緊縮調整。Bloomberg週五較晚的利率報導指出，交換市場對12月9日的升息定價約為20個基點，高於非農公布前的19個基點與週四的17個基點。延伸至2027年中的合約反映約46個基點的緊縮，高於公布前的44個基點及週四的38個基點。這些調整遠小於2年期殖利率最初的跳升幅度。

明年將取得政策投票權的Daly認為，很可能仍需進一步緊縮，但未確定時間與幅度。她支持9月升息及10月暫停，並主張審慎推進，因為最終所需的緊縮程度仍不明確。她特別關切不含住房的服務通膨：這類價格受關稅或能源成本的直接影響較小，降幅卻不如官員預期。她樂見就業強勁，但表示勞工薪資未能跟上通膨。對於股市下跌，她認為過程有序，預期短期僅會對成長造成部分拖累，並指出AI以外的企業抱持審慎樂觀態度。

紐約聯準銀行總裁John Williams另在法蘭克福強調，現階段要持續蒐集資訊。他認為通膨過高，但通膨預期仍穩定錨定，薪資增長也與2%目標相符。貨幣政策的作用，是防止相對價格衝擊演變成更廣泛、更持久的通膨。聖路易聯準銀行總裁Alberto Musalem週五另提出警訊，認為AI投資可能推升短期通膨；他將於2028年取得政策投票權。這些談話保留了進一步緊縮的理由，但未形成對緊縮步調的共識。

密西根大學11月消費者調查初值則帶來另一組需求與通膨訊號。信心指數由10月的48.0升至51.0，高於路透調查共識48.0。現況指數由46.7升至51.0，預期指數由48.8升至50.9。未來一年通膨預期由4.7%降至4.3%，長期通膨預期由3.5%降至3.4%。

調查於10月20日至11月2日進行，早於期中選舉，反映的是家戶投票前的心態。負擔能力仍是重大疑慮：約57%受訪者主動提及高物價侵蝕生活水準，2月時為46%，整體信心也仍比2月低約10%。調查主任Joanne Hsu另指出，民眾擔心AI相關股票估值能否持續。

利率調整之際，股市反彈並不平均。標普500指數上漲0.31%至7,376.86，那斯達克100上漲1.35%，半導體類股上漲4.21%；但那斯達克一週仍下跌4.91%，半導體指數下跌12.15%。VIX下跌9.01%至25.64，仍較一週前高32.03%。StoneX的Fawad Razaqzada認為，科技股反彈主要來自空頭回補與逢低買盤，支出及監管疑慮仍未解決。美元指數上漲0.74%至102.3，黃金期貨下跌0.94%至每盎司$4,074.90。高盛因利率較高、能源價格不確定，將年底金價預測由$4,650下修至$4,150。

財政前景則出現更明確的融資期限。美國銀行、巴克萊與摩根士丹利策略師目前預期，美國財政部將於2月中下旬觸及法定債務上限；美國銀行先前估計約在5月。政府距離$41.1兆上限的餘裕已不足$8,000億，而財政部預估第一季淨借款約$8,000億，並計畫在3月底保有$1兆現金餘額。

觸及上限後將啟動非常措施，估計可額外提供$3,000億至$3,500億的空間。若國會未採取行動，策略師估計現金與非常措施的額度將在8月至11月間耗盡。Bloomberg報導，國庫券殖利率曲線目前尚未反映明顯疑慮。影響將透過財政部現金管理傳導：初期動用現金、減少國庫券供給，會增加銀行體系準備金並壓低隔夜利率；上限問題解決後重建現金餘額，則會逆轉這些效果。若僵局拖長，也可能延後增加較長天期債券發行的安排。

## AI債市依借款人與融資管道分化

週五亞洲交易時段，科技股重新評價的壓力延伸至美元債。軟銀2032年到期債券下跌0.9美分，創十週最大跌幅，股價一度下跌16%。交易員表示，亞洲美元債殖利率溢酬擴大至少3個基點。CreditSights分析師Zerlina Zeng形容，債市賣壓仍屬溫和，先前美國公債殖利率下降緩和了整體殖利率的壓力，部分買盤也在10月下跌後，重返仍正常履約的中國房地產債。

區域債市走弱之前，亞洲股市經歷重挫。台灣加權指數收跌4.5%，進入熊市；南韓Kospi一度下跌8.8%，觸發熔斷。券商及資產管理業者指出，台灣與香港的高資產客戶出現追繳保證金壓力。這些壓力發生在美國科技股反彈之前。至美國收盤，整體投資級與高收益債利差大致持平，強勢貨幣計價的新興市場債利差小幅收窄，總體市場已較稍早亞洲時段穩定。

歐洲公司債持續受惠於近期新債提供的補償。據Bloomberg報導，Meta歐元債平均上漲約1.6%，Alphabet歐元債約上漲0.9%。Alphabet給予的新債發行溢酬，約為今年以來歐元公司債平均水準的兩倍。投資級iTraxx信用違約交換指數週五上升約1個基點，投機級指數上升4個基點，均低於10月下旬高點。L&G的Colin Reedie表示交易有序，債市下一個重大問題，是AI若放緩將如何影響實體經濟。

Meta籌資的新報導顯示，借款人正投入大量心力爭取融資。公司與承銷銀行在兩天內向美國及歐洲約500家機構投資人推介，財務長Susan Li也參與部分通話。知情人士表示，Meta告訴投資人，至少在明年第二季之前，沒有再發行無擔保債的計畫，並說明將如何分散資金來源、讓AI投資產生回報。這番說明涵蓋未來融資頻率及單筆交易規模。

先前報導擬出售約$5億資料中心貸款組合的銀行，現已確認為ING。組合包括新墨西哥州Stargate計畫的$2,500萬貸款權益，該計畫涉及OpenAI、軟銀與Oracle。賣方身分揭露了哪家銀行正在降低曝險，出售程序則仍在進行。

歐洲監理機關也考慮深入檢視同一融資鏈。知情人士表示，歐洲央行已在內部及與銀行的討論中，提出審查資料中心放款的構想；現場檢查是可能方式之一，重點包括預估現金流、擔保品估值與潛在違約的提存。範圍尚未確定，一名知情人士表示，規模會小於先前的槓桿融資審查。歐洲央行拒絕評論這項可能的檢查。

Christine Lagarde在週五公布的另一封信中表示，歐洲央行正在關注AI融資與金融穩定，指出債務上升、交叉持股、企業相互承諾及私募市場參與，使關係更為複雜。監理焦點在於授信品質與相互連結的曝險。歐洲銀行管理局主席上月估計，銀行對整體資訊與通訊科技業的曝險不到歐盟銀行總曝險的4%；這個分類涵蓋範圍比AI更廣。

計畫層面的政策討論也更具體。參議員Martin Heinrich致函土地管理局，詢問橫跨美國西部六州、占地超過17,000英畝的至少15項資料中心與相關基礎設施提案。這封信是在6月內華達州一處88英畝用地獲准後提出；他預計明年將出任參議院能源與自然資源委員會主席。OpenAI則承諾加強揭露噪音、用水與用電等社區影響，並承諾在尖峰時段降低用電、向電網回送電力，以及在人力供給允許下訂定在地招聘目標。這些監督與營運措施，都是因應地方反對聲浪所提出的回應。

審視趨嚴之際，新資金仍持續流入。週日刊出的報導引述知情人士指出，OpenAI已完成一輪募資的首批約$110億，估值達$1.25兆。其餘資金預計在隨後數週到位，整輪規模最高可能達$200億。

AI以外，私募貸款機構仍在安排大額承諾。Apollo為Thrive Holdings收購ADT提供約$96億債務融資承諾，Blackstone則為歐洲直接貸款策略募得約€130億。另一方面，Bloomberg看到的一封信顯示，Arini主要信用避險基金10月虧損19.7%，今年以來跌幅擴大至32%。機構募資、收購融資承諾與投資人虧損同時出現，反映私募及槓桿信用市場內部的處境差異甚大。

## 海外數據使政策預期分歧

加拿大就業報告讓當地利率市場朝美國的相反方向調整。10月就業減少4,700人，連續第三個月下滑，市場原預期增加1.5萬人。失業率升至6.7%，高於市場共識與前值的6.5%。總就業僅小幅減少，背後卻是民間受僱人數減少5.25萬人，幾乎被公部門增加的4.96萬人抵銷。

加拿大2年期殖利率一度觸及3.175%，之後最低降至3.113%。交易員將加拿大央行12月升息的隱含機率，由週四約40%下調至33%。長期僱用全職員工的時薪年增率由2.3%放緩至2%，低於預測的2.1%。青年失業率跳升0.7個百分點至13.7%；失業者中，已求職至少27週的比率為23.7%，高於一年前的21.5%。

疲弱集中在民間經濟的部分產業。批發與零售業10月減少2.88萬人，年減11.31萬人；營建業則增加1.56萬人，年增4.7萬人。BMO的Benjamin Reitzes表示，就業連續三個月減少，應使央行審慎考量進一步升息的時間。

加拿大Ivey調查呈現不同的企業觀察。經季節調整的採購經理人指數由58.2小升至58.3，高於50的擴張門檻，就業分項由56.5升至58.3。價格指數由82.8降至81.7，但仍偏高。採購經理人調查顯示持續擴張、就業情況轉強，加拿大統計局家戶調查則記錄到就業減少。兩項調查涵蓋的群體與衡量概念不同，各自反映的擴張與就業減少訊號仍同時存在。

日本公債在亞洲時段大漲，全球股市下跌帶動避險需求，也降低近期升息預期。10年期殖利率下降12個基點至2.635%，5年期下降14個基點至2.05%，2年期下降13個基點至1.725%。Bloomberg亞洲時段報導指出，隔夜指數交換反映日本央行12月升息機率約52%，低於前一天的80%。另一篇週五報導則引用東京市場約68%的機率，是波動市況下不同觀察時點的數字。SMBC日興證券的Ataru Okumura警告，股市恐慌期間，投資人聚焦於緊縮可能提早結束，殖利率下滑幅度可能過大。

薪資數據則強化了日本持續推進政策正常化的國內依據。9月名目現金薪資年增4.6%，為1997年以來最快；實質薪資年增2.2%，高於市場共識1.3%及8月修正後的1.6%，已連續九個月增加。排除獎金、加班與抽樣扭曲後，一項較穩定的全職員工薪資指標增長3.1%，創紀錄新高。

總數之下仍有重要差異。基本薪資增幅由3.8%放緩至3.7%，加班薪資增幅由4.9%降至3.6%；特別給付則大增32.6%，遠高於8月的1.8%，主管部會將異常增幅歸因於統計因素。因此，整體薪資轉強既包含持續性的基礎薪資增長，也受到特別給付異常增加推升。三菱綜合研究所的Yasunari Tanaka預期，明年春季薪資談判增幅約5%，大致與2026年相當；最大工會聯合組織則已呼籲提出約6%的加薪要求。

日本央行總裁植田和男週五在華盛頓的國際貨幣基金組織場合表示，基礎通膨已達2%，但能否持續仍不確定。他指出，2%通膨尚未成為社會常態，接下來的任務是透過適當政策調整，讓這個水準維持多年，未對下次升息提出具體指引。銀行放款增長超過5%，創三十年最快，他將此與溫和通膨下企業風險承擔意願復甦相連結。

日本另公布一筆反映前期市況的大額投資損失。政府年金投資基金GPIF在截至9月的一季虧損1.7%、即¥5.253兆，為六季以來首次負報酬。外國債券報酬率為負6.52%，國內債券為負1.80%，日本股票上漲3.71%，海外股票下跌1.86%。該報告期間，10年期美國公債殖利率上升81個基點，日本指標公債殖利率上升約38個基點，美元兌日圓下跌逾3%。基金資產為¥314.4兆。

首相高市早苗提議，將日本央行加快出售ETF所增加的繳庫款，用於經濟安全投資。日本央行已宣布，從1月起將年度出售額由¥3,300億提高至¥8,600億；Bloomberg Economics估計，加快出售可能讓每年繳庫款增加約¥8,000億。高市希望將資金納入跨年度特別會計。政府計畫先發行過橋債券籌資，而償還這類債券須明確列出未來財源，因此預期增加的繳庫款成為這項融資提案的重要部分。

中國10年期公債殖利率盤中降至紀錄低點1.58%，下降約1個基點，30年期則在2.03%左右。避險需求與充裕流動性支撐債市。法國農業信貸銀行的Jeffrey Zhang表示，先前信用疑慮消退後，投資人正重建現券部位。渣打銀行的Becky Liu認為，短期進一步寬鬆空間有限，但預期較低且更穩定的銀行間利率，將支持殖利率再小幅下降。

英國央行前一天將利率升至4%後，首席經濟學家Huw Pill提出後續政策的條件：若成長停滯、第二輪通膨威脅減弱，利率可能維持不變或下調。他形容這次升息是預防性措施，預期到春季會有更清楚的證據，顯示薪資與物價如何回應能源衝擊。總裁Andrew Bailey另表示，若中東和解取得持久進展，可能改變政策前景。報導Pill週五談話時，市場給予下月再升息約60%的機率。

房市數據顯示借款成本帶來壓力，不同指標卻有分歧。Lloyds公布10月房價月跌0.6%，市場原預期上升0.1%；年跌1.2%，為2023年10月以來最大年跌幅。Nationwide則顯示月持平、年增0.5%。法國勞動統計又顯示另一項家戶壓力：第三季民間部門實質薪資較一年前下降1.1%。

歐洲央行首席經濟學家Philip Lane週五表示，官員正在12月會議前蒐集資訊，希望抑制能源衝擊擴散至其他價格。週六刊出的訪談中，Lagarde表示未來幾季通膨仍將偏高，若要改變預期的政策方向，必須有重大新資訊，但她未承諾12月升息。她指出，多年期薪資協議與企業薪酬預期，尚未出現超出既有預測所納入第二輪效應的變化。

歐洲央行領導人選角逐也有進展：週五截止前，正式獲提名的只有Klaas Knot與Pablo Hernandez de Cos。現任國際清算銀行總經理的de Cos在週六訪談中提出自己的政策看法：第二輪效應尚未出現，但能源成本若持續偏高，仍須保持警覺。他也警告，利率上升會提高高赤字與高負債的償債成本。

智利10月CPI為當地升息討論提供新證據。通膨年增4.5%，略低於預測的4.6%，月增0.5%。運輸價格上漲2%、能源上漲2.7%、食品與非酒精飲料上漲1%，服飾則下跌4.1%；排除食品與能源的通膨當月持平。數據顯示供給成本貢獻顯著，基礎物價的月度變化則溫和得多。

捷克對升息的政治分歧也升高。總理Andrej Babis抨擊週四的升息，認為這將提高家戶與企業借款成本，卻無法影響全球能源價格。央行說明，其關切的是這些成本擴散至更廣泛的通膨與預期；總裁Ales Michl則堅持政策將維持獨立。

## 重整協商惡化，主權風險升高

Braskem債權人拒絕一項$38億債轉股提案後，公司取得資本支持的前景轉差。熟悉本週紐約協商的人士表示，Petrobras與IG4已撤回按當時討論條件注資的提議。這項不具約束力的方案原擬由股東提供$14億資本，條件是完成換債。協商仍在繼續，各方須在11月下旬前達成協議，聲請破產保護也再度列為替代選項。

凡需Petrobras支持的交易，都必須取得其董事會同意。其他知情人士表示，董事對目前條件抱持懷疑，將予以否決。Braskem表示會透過正式管道揭露進展；Petrobras與IG4未立即回應。Braskem美國存託憑證一度下跌30%，之後收斂跌幅。長期現金消耗與石化價格疲弱之後，爭議焦點在於股東願以何種條件投入新資本。

Rhodium Group本週為美國商會發布的另一項研究，則指出中國化工產能過剩威脅海外生產商。研究員Jeremy Smith將問題連結至產能擴張，以及2021年後房地產相關需求流失，迫使更多產品銷往海外。他認為，中國制止價格戰、升級設施的措施，恐難解除外國競爭者面臨的壓力，並呼籲在整條價值鏈上協調。這項研究從產業層面解釋了化工業持續承受的競爭壓力。

Brightspeed正與債權人討論籌措$20億至$30億新資本，以處理約$100億債務與光纖網路建置成本。知情人士表示，金額及融資將在法院內或庭外安排，均尚未確定。這家由Apollo支持的公司近期已警告，其持續經營能力存在疑慮。

不同層級證券的價格，顯示資本結構內的回收預期差距甚大。約$26億延後動用定期貸款週五報價約為面額每$1的66.25美分，約$25億以債付息（PIK）貸款則在17.25美分附近，兩者均於2031年到期。公司光纖業務銷售年增16%，4月曾宣布可提供光纖服務的地點超過300萬處。即使營運增長，跨20州的擴張仍需大量資本。2024年重整已削減$11億債務並提供$37億新資本，同時在擔保借款中建立不同的償付順位。

塞內加爾計畫換債，可能因此被信評機構認定違約。穆迪的Lucie Villa表示，即使塞內加爾繼續按期付款，穆迪仍極可能將換債歸類為困境交換。該國正尋求IMF董事會批准一項$22億計畫，Villa警告，修訂2026年預算的僵局可能延誤批准。

塞內加爾在摩根大通指數中的主權利差約1,469個基點，5年期違約保護成本為2,145個基點，較9月1日宣布債務調整與IMF計畫時上升逾33%。近期付款包括11月23日須支付2033年到期證券的$3,125萬利息，以及12月10日另到期應付的$3,875萬。

阿根廷政治不確定性疊加全球風險偏好下降，使美元債利差逼近困境水準。指標2035年到期債券殖利率由前一週末的12.67%，升至週五的13.77%，債價下跌逾3美分。摩根大通一項指標顯示，該國主權風險溢酬在本週前四天擴大近140個基點後達928個基點。阿根廷國內市場週五因銀行假日休市，紐約交易的阿根廷債券則收斂部分跌幅。

貝萊德的Pablo Goldberg表示，投資人比預期更早開始反映明年總統大選。PPI的Pedro Siaba Serrate建立的債券價格模型，推估Javier Milei連任機率約45%，低於7月約90%。這項模型估計的變化，伴隨市場對未來能否繼續取得美國支持的疑慮，包括2025年安排的$200億換匯額度。阿根廷持續維持財政盈餘，並受惠於強勁出口，但投資人質疑政治支持能否持久，也關注疑似官方買進本地債券對外匯存底的影響。

週日的區域報導呈現對華府反應的不同看法。Grit Capital的Walter Stoeppelwerth預期川普會繼續支持Milei；AllianceBernstein的Katrina Butt預期國會審視將增加，但指出換匯額度是透過行政權限實施。談及委內瑞拉，她指出審視也正加強，投資人仍等待原預期6月公布的債務可持續性分析；這是重整數百億美元違約債券的先決條件。巴拉圭方面，政治危機進一步發展，前總統Santiago Pena遭參議院罷黜後，因涉嫌涉及Ueno Bank倒閉而被起訴。這些是區域內各自不同的政治與債務重整風險變化。

## 週末能源事件使外交前景更複雜

週五油價大致持平，但一週已明顯下跌。布蘭特原油期貨上漲0.03%至每桶$98.32，一週下跌13.32%；WTI上漲0.34%至$90.83，一週下跌12.76%。週五報導指出，伊朗正審議一項涉及核計畫的提案，並願意討論先前排除於談判之外的議題。卡達持續斡旋，外交突破仍有待條件成熟。

週末隨後出現新的實體供應中斷。伊拉克Khor Mor天然氣田週日遭無人機攻擊，液化石油氣儲槽被擊中起火，營運因而暫停。初步報導稱無人死亡，攻擊者身分及停產將持續多久均尚未確認。停產使區域電力系統減少約2.8吉瓦發電能力，對伊拉克庫德地區供電影響重大。

伊拉克外交部長Fuad Hussein另表示，巴格達已與華府達成諒解，意在讓伊拉克石油透過荷莫茲海峽靠近阿曼的航路出口。他估計，出口受阻造成約$600億損失。伊拉克能源官員表示，10月出口約每日350萬桶，高於9月的265萬桶，這項增加發生在週日宣布安排之前。這項新通行安排如何落實，仍未解決。

海事安全消息則較不明朗。伊朗國營媒體稱兩艘油輪觸雷、第三艘船起火；美軍代表另表示，在執行封鎖期間有商船受損。路透無法獨立核實所報導的襲擊。英國海上貿易行動辦公室UKMTO通報，阿拉伯聯合大公國Khor Fakkan附近約18海里處發生散裝貨輪事件，但尚未確認不同描述是否指同一事件。川普週日表示，若能達成有力協議，美國極不可能再發動大規模攻擊；他也討論了若戰事重啟，可能攻擊的基礎設施目標。

沙烏地阿拉伯當局表示，在利雅德及該國東部上空攔截飛彈，碎片損壞沙烏地阿美一棟行政大樓數層樓的窗戶，損害有限。青年運動聲稱攻擊沙烏地目標，沙烏地當局則表示已對葉門發射設施採取軍事行動。已確認的阿美損害位於辦公室，初步報導尚未確認當地有生產、煉油或出口中斷。市場即將重開之際，這些週末事件使能源安全局勢仍不穩定。

## 後續市場焦點

美國10月CPI將於11月10日美東時間上午8時30分公布，是強勁非農就業之後，檢驗12月利率前景的下一項重大數據。市場共識預期整體物價月增0.3%，前值為0.6%；核心物價月增0.2%，前值為0.3%。Bloomberg前瞻指出，因2025年10月數據在政府關門期間未發布，美國勞工統計局這次不會公布年增率比較。因此，商品、住房與其他服務的月度組成將是判斷重點，尤其Daly已表達對非住房服務通膨持續偏高的關切。週五的生產者物價報告則預期顯示，通膨年增率加快至6.6%。

週一紐約聯準銀行消費者預期調查，將在密西根大學通膨預期下降後，提供另一項家戶通膨指標。Michelle Bowman、Austan Goolsbee與Tom Barkin預定11月9日發言，Christopher Waller與Lorie Logan則於11月10日登場，可觀察官員如何權衡較強就業與收緊的金融情勢。11月就業報告將於12月4日公布，早於12月9日政策決定。

財政部季度再融資標售，將圍繞通膨數據與週三退伍軍人節現券市場休市展開。已公告的週一$580億3年期標售率先登場，週二為10年期，週四為30年期。週五利率報導顯示，3年期殖利率約4.59%，上次標售得標殖利率為4.932%。公債先上漲、再因就業報告回吐部分漲幅之後，這些標售將檢驗需求，而後兩場之間少了通常的週中現券交易日。

企業籌資需求仍大。交易商預期未來一週美國高評級債發行約$400億。歐洲供給調查涵蓋的市場不同：承銷團聯絡人士估計，包括歐元、英鎊及離岸美元交易的廣義企業發債總額約€133億至€161億；另一項高評級債調查則有75%受訪者預期至少€300億。科技股下跌後，Anthropic擬議上市也面臨估值重估。近期歐元新債次級市場回升之際，借款人能以何種條件取得新資金，仍同樣重要。

歐元區財長將於11月9日評估Knot與de Cos，歐洲央行總裁最終人選由歐洲領袖決定。這也屬於更廣泛的執委會人事調整，涉及Isabel Schnabel與Philip Lane離任；11月13日及11月26日至27日領袖會議，提供後續協商機會。英國11月12日GDP報告預期季增0.7%，將進一步顯示Pill視為後續政策關鍵的經濟韌性。日本即將公布的央行意見摘要與家戶支出數據，則有助於判斷強勁薪資能否支持持久內需。

美國收盤後，決策官員持續區分AI投資的即時成本與仍不確定的後續效益。IMF總裁Kristalina Georgieva警告，AI帶動的成長若放緩，將改變央行所處環境，並可能產生金融穩定風險。週一上午在雪梨，澳洲央行經濟學家Sarah Hunter表示，基礎設施建設正增加需求與成本壓力，但澳洲整體統計尚未顯示顯著生產力效益。她指出，部分受AI影響的職業，徵才廣告僅初步呈現疲弱。支出是否放緩、融資是否更具選擇性，以及生產力能否改善，仍是判斷這波投資如何影響通膨與成長的核心。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries surrendered part of their weekly rally as stronger U.S. hiring and firmer monthly wage growth reinforced expectations of another Federal Reserve rate increase in December. The retreat was concentrated in shorter maturities: the two-year yield rose 4.92 basis points to 4.5115%, while the 10-year added 2.27 basis points to 4.8574%. Much of the week's advance survived a payroll report that challenged expectations of a slowing economy, with investors still weighing the consequences of weaker technology valuations and a less certain artificial-intelligence investment pipeline.

October payrolls increased 165,000, accompanied by substantial upward revisions, and headline unemployment fell to 4.1%. San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said the solid labor market gave policymakers room to address persistent inflation. The report also exposed a less comfortable position for people struggling to find sufficient work: broader underemployment increased, involuntary part-time employment rose, and jobless spells lengthened.

The recovery in risk appetite was selective. Semiconductor stocks rebounded 4.21%, but U.S. investment-grade and high-yield spreads were little changed. SoftBank's bonds weakened in Asian trading, while European corporate debt held up better as generous terms on recent technology issues supported their performance. Outside the AI financing cycle, Braskem's restructuring negotiations deteriorated and Brightspeed sought as much as $3 billion in fresh capital. These borrower-specific funding problems remained consequential even as the broader market stabilized.

## Payroll Strength Checks the Treasury Rally

The employment release interrupted a market that had entered Friday positioned for further gains. In Bloomberg's intraday account, the two-year Treasury yield rose as much as 9 basis points to 4.55% before retreating toward 4.51%. The initial selloff faded as the session progressed, leaving the most persistent adjustment in maturities sensitive to the next few Fed decisions.

The closing curve flattened through that selloff. Five-year yields rose 4.04 basis points to 4.6449%, while the 30-year increased 1.06 basis points to 5.2645%. The two- to 10-year spread narrowed 2.65 basis points to 34.59 basis points, and the two- to 30-year gap contracted 3.86 basis points to 75.3 basis points. The smaller long-end reversal left the 10-year yield 7.15 basis points lower over the week and 42.41 basis points lower over the month. Two-year yields were down 7.61 basis points over the week; the 30-year's weekly decline was 4.37 basis points.

Real yields accounted for the larger part of Friday's 10-year increase. The corresponding TIPS yield rose 1.5 basis points to 2.6127%, while inflation compensation increased 0.77 basis point to 2.2447%. Across the week, the relationship was different: real yields rose 2.82 basis points and the breakeven fell 9.97 basis points. The week's nominal rally therefore continued to depend on lower inflation compensation even after Friday's stronger employment news. Over the month, real yields fell 29.91 basis points and the breakeven declined 12.5 basis points.

The payroll improvement extended beyond a single headline. The Bureau of Labor Statistics raised August's gain to 186,000 from 133,000 and September's to 60,000 from 29,000, adding a combined 84,000 jobs to the earlier estimates. October's 165,000 increase compared with a 48,000 monthly average over the preceding 12 months. The pre-release calendar consensus was 65,000. Private payrolls rose 159,000, against expectations of 64,000 and a revised September gain of 78,000, while government employment increased 6,000 after a revised 18,000 decline.

Professional and business services supplied 70,000 jobs, compared with a 15,000 monthly average over the prior year. Technical services added 33,000, administration 28,000 and management 9,000. Health care added 42,000, above its prior-year average of 31,000, including 16,000 in hospitals and 11,000 in home health. Transportation and warehousing increased 25,000, led by 17,000 courier jobs and 4,000 in air transportation.

Manufacturing added 19,000 jobs, compared with a 5,000 consensus and a revised 13,000 in September. Electronics contributed 7,000, with machinery and primary metals each adding 4,000. Bloomberg reported that computer and electronic-product manufacturers recorded their largest employment gain in four years. Nonresidential construction continued hiring, although residential-building losses weighed on broader construction employment. Information and financial activities, sectors that had experienced job losses alongside rapid AI adoption, showed tentative stabilization.

Monthly pay growth was stronger than expected, even as the annual pace remained subdued by recent standards. Average hourly earnings increased $0.14, or 0.4%, to $38.00, exceeding the 0.3% monthly consensus. Annual growth was 3.1%, above expectations of 2.9% but below September's revised 3.2%. Production and nonsupervisory earnings also rose 0.4%, or $0.12, to $32.75. Average weekly hours held at 34.4. Manufacturing hours stayed at 40.5, while overtime edged up to 3.1 hours; production and nonsupervisory hours slipped 0.1 to 33.8.

The household survey showed both wider participation and more underutilization. Headline U-3 unemployment fell to 4.1% from 4.2%, against expectations of no change. Participation rose to 61.9% from 61.8%, and the employment-to-population ratio increased to 59.3% from 59.2%. However, U-6, the broader labor-underutilization measure, rose to 7.9% from 7.6%. The number working part-time for economic reasons increased 339,000 to 4.840 million. Median unemployment duration reached 11.9 weeks, the longest since 2021. Stronger hiring thus coexisted with increasing difficulty for some workers in obtaining full-time employment or moving back into work.

Fed pricing moved modestly toward additional restraint. Bloomberg's later Friday rates account put swap-implied tightening for December 9 at about 20 basis points, compared with 19 basis points before payrolls and 17 basis points on Thursday. Contracts extending to mid-2027 priced about 46 basis points of tightening, up from 44 before the release and 38 on Thursday. Those changes were considerably smaller than the initial jump in two-year yields.

Daly, who becomes a voting policymaker next year, said further tightening was likely, while leaving its timing and extent open. She supported both September's increase and October's pause and favored a deliberate approach because the eventual degree of restraint remained uncertain. Her particular concern was services inflation excluding housing, which had failed to ease as much as officials expected even though it is less directly driven by tariffs or energy costs. She welcomed hiring strength but said workers' pay was failing to keep pace with inflation. She also described the equity selloff as orderly and expected only some near-term growth drag, citing cautious optimism among businesses beyond AI.

New York Fed President John Williams, speaking separately in Frankfurt, emphasized gathering information. He judged inflation too high but said expectations remained well anchored and wage growth was consistent with the 2% objective. Policy's role was to prevent relative-price shocks from becoming broader, more persistent inflation. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem added a distinct caution on Friday: AI investment could contribute to near-term inflation. Musalem is scheduled to vote on policy in 2028. Together, the remarks preserved a case for further tightening without establishing agreement on its pace.

November's preliminary University of Michigan survey supplied a different mix of demand and inflation evidence. Sentiment rose to 51.0 from October's 48.0, exceeding the 48.0 Reuters consensus. Current conditions improved to 51.0 from 46.7, and expectations to 50.9 from 48.8. Expected inflation over the next year declined to 4.3% from 4.7%; longer-term expectations fell to 3.4% from 3.5%.

The survey covered October 20 through November 2, before the midterm election. Its improvement therefore described household attitudes entering the vote. Affordability remained a substantial concern: about 57% of respondents volunteered that high prices had eroded their living standards, compared with 46% in February, and sentiment remained about 10% below February's level. Survey director Joanne Hsu also identified concern about the sustainability of AI-related equity valuations.

Equities recovered unevenly alongside the rates adjustment. The S&P 500 rose 0.31% to 7,376.86, the Nasdaq 100 gained 1.35%, and semiconductor stocks advanced 4.21%. The Nasdaq still lost 4.91% over the week and the semiconductor index 12.15%. The VIX fell 9.01% to 25.64 but remained 32.03% above its week-earlier level. StoneX's Fawad Razaqzada attributed the technology rebound largely to short covering and bargain hunting, with spending and regulatory concerns unresolved. The Dollar Index rose 0.74% to 102.3, and gold futures fell 0.94% to $4,074.90 an ounce. Goldman Sachs lowered its year-end gold forecast to $4,150 from $4,650, citing higher interest rates and uncertain energy prices.

The fiscal outlook acquired a more specific financing deadline. Bank of America, Barclays and Morgan Stanley strategists now expect Treasury to reach its statutory debt limit in mid- to late February; Bank of America had previously expected around May. The government has less than $800 billion of room under the $41.1 trillion ceiling, against Treasury's projected net borrowing of roughly $800 billion in Q1 and a planned end-March cash balance of $1 trillion.

Reaching the ceiling would begin a period of extraordinary measures, estimated to provide $300 billion-$350 billion of additional capacity. Strategists put the later exhaustion of cash and those measures between August and November, absent congressional action. Bloomberg reported little current concern in the bill curve. The funding consequences would unfold through Treasury's cash management: drawing down cash and reducing bill supply initially adds banking-system reserves and depresses overnight rates, while rebuilding the cash balance after a resolution reverses those effects. A prolonged standoff could also delay a shift toward more longer-maturity issuance.

## AI Credit Separates by Borrower and Funding Channel

Friday's Asian trading extended the technology repricing into dollar debt. SoftBank's 2032 bond fell 0.9 cent, its largest decline in 10 weeks, and its shares dropped as much as 16%. Traders reported Asian dollar-bond yield premiums widening at least 3 basis points. CreditSights analyst Zerlina Zeng described a measured credit selloff, with the preceding decline in Treasury yields cushioning all-in yields and some buyers returning to performing Chinese property credits after October's losses.

The regional move followed a severe Asian equity session. Taiwan's benchmark closed down 4.5% and entered a bear market, while South Korea's Kospi fell as much as 8.8%, triggering a circuit breaker. Brokers and managers reported margin calls among wealthy clients in Taiwan and Hong Kong. Those pressures preceded the U.S. technology rebound. By the U.S. close, broad investment-grade and high-yield spreads were little changed and hard-currency emerging-market spreads were modestly tighter, showing a more settled aggregate market than the earlier Asian trading.

European corporate bonds continued to benefit from the compensation offered on recent issues. Meta's euro debt had gained about 1.6% on average and Alphabet's about 0.9%, according to Bloomberg. Alphabet had paid about twice the year-to-date average new-issue premium for euro corporate bonds. The high-grade iTraxx credit-default-swap index rose about 1 basis point Friday and its speculative-grade counterpart 4 basis points, with both below late-October highs. L&G's Colin Reedie described orderly trading and said the next major credit question was the effect of any AI slowdown on the real economy.

New reporting on Meta's fundraising showed how much effort borrowers were making to secure access. The company and its banks pitched roughly 500 institutional investors across the U.S. and Europe over two days, with Chief Financial Officer Susan Li joining some calls. People familiar with the discussions said Meta told investors it did not plan to return for unsecured debt until at least Q2 next year. It also explained how it intended to diversify funding and generate returns from AI investment. That guidance addresses the frequency of future financing as well as the size of an individual deal.

The bank selling the previously reported roughly $500 million data-center loan portfolio was identified as ING. The portfolio includes a $25 million interest in the New Mexico Stargate project involving OpenAI, SoftBank and Oracle. Identifying the lender added information about who was reducing exposure, while the sale process itself remained underway.

European supervisors were considering a closer examination of the same financing chain. People familiar with the discussions said the ECB had floated a review of data-center lending internally and with banks. On-site inspections were one possible approach, focusing on projected cash flows, collateral valuations and provisioning for potential defaults. The scope had not been decided, and one person said it would be narrower than the earlier leveraged-finance review. The ECB declined to comment on the prospective examination.

In a letter published Friday, Christine Lagarde separately said the ECB was monitoring AI financing and financial stability. She identified rising debt, interlinked ownership, mutual commitments among companies and private-market involvement as sources of complexity. That focus concerns underwriting and interconnected exposures. The European Banking Authority's chairman had estimated last month that banks' entire information and communications technology exposure, a category broader than AI, represented less than 4% of EU bank exposure.

Project policy also became more specific. Senator Martin Heinrich asked the Bureau of Land Management about at least 15 proposals for data centers and related infrastructure covering more than 17,000 acres across six Western states. His letter followed June's approval of an 88-acre Nevada site, and he is poised to chair the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee next year. OpenAI, meanwhile, promised greater disclosure of community impacts, including noise, water and power demand, and pledged to reduce electricity use at peak times, return power to the grid and set local hiring goals where workforce availability permits. These were proposed oversight and operating responses to local opposition.

Fresh funding continued alongside the scrutiny. In an account published Sunday, people familiar with the matter said OpenAI had closed roughly $11 billion in the initial part of a round valuing it at $1.25 trillion. The remainder, which could bring the round to as much as $20 billion, was expected over the following weeks. The distinction between the completed first portion and the prospective balance matters to the amount of capital already available.

Outside AI, private lenders were still arranging large commitments. Apollo provided about $9.6 billion of debt commitments for Thrive Holdings' acquisition of ADT, while Blackstone raised around EUR13 billion for its European direct-lending strategy. At the same time, Arini's main credit hedge fund lost 19.7% in October, taking its year-to-date decline to 32%, according to a letter seen by Bloomberg. The combination of institutional fundraising, acquisition commitments and investor losses pointed to sharply differing conditions within private and leveraged credit.

## Overseas Data Pull Policy Expectations Apart

Canada's labor release moved its rates market in the opposite direction to the U.S. Employment fell 4,700 in October, a third consecutive monthly decline, against expectations of a 15,000 increase. Unemployment rose to 6.7%, compared with a 6.5% consensus and previous reading. The small net employment loss concealed a 52,500 decline in private-sector employees, almost offset by 49,600 additional public-sector workers.

Canadian two-year yields fell as low as 3.113% after trading as high as 3.175%. Traders reduced the implied probability of a December Bank of Canada increase to 33% from about 40% Thursday. Permanent full-time employees' hourly wage growth slowed to 2% annually from 2.3%, below the 2.1% forecast. Youth unemployment jumped 0.7 percentage point to 13.7%, and 23.7% of unemployed people had been looking for work for at least 27 weeks, up from 21.5% a year earlier.

The weakness was concentrated in parts of the private economy. Wholesale and retail employment fell 28,800 in October and 113,100 over the year. Construction instead added 15,600 jobs and was up 47,000 annually. BMO's Benjamin Reitzes said three successive monthly losses should make the central bank cautious about the timing of further increases.

Canada's Ivey survey offered a different business observation. The seasonally adjusted purchasing managers' index edged up to 58.3 from 58.2, above the 50 expansion threshold, and its employment component rose to 58.3 from 56.5. The prices index eased to 81.7 from 82.8 but remained elevated. Purchasing managers were reporting continued expansion and stronger employment conditions in their survey, while Statistics Canada's household survey recorded job losses. The two measures cover different populations and concepts; neither eliminates the other's signal.

Japan's government bonds rallied sharply in Asian trading as the global equity retreat brought haven demand and reduced near-term tightening expectations. The 10-year yield fell 12 basis points to 2.635%, the five-year 14 basis points to 2.05%, and the two-year 13 basis points to 1.725%. Bloomberg's Asian-session account put overnight-indexed-swap pricing for a December BOJ increase at about 52%, down from 80% the previous day. A separate Friday account cited about 68% in Tokyo, reflecting a different observation of a volatile market. SMBC Nikko's Ataru Okumura warned that the yield decline could be excessive as investors focused on an early end to tightening during the equity panic.

The wage release strengthened the domestic case for continued normalization. September nominal cash earnings rose 4.6% annually, the fastest since 1997, while real earnings rose 2.2%, above the 1.3% consensus and August's revised 1.6%. Real pay increased for a ninth consecutive month. A more stable measure excluding bonuses, overtime and sampling distortions rose a record 3.1% for full-time workers.

There were important differences beneath the headline. Basic pay growth eased to 3.7% from 3.8%, and overtime earnings growth slowed to 3.6% from 4.9%. Special payments surged 32.6%, compared with 1.8% in August, an exceptional movement the ministry attributed to a statistical quirk. The stronger total therefore included both sustained underlying wage gains and an unusually large special-payments contribution. Mitsubishi Research Institute's Yasunari Tanaka expected next year's wage negotiations to deliver increases around 5%, broadly matching 2026, while the largest union federation had called for demands around 6%.

Speaking at the IMF in Washington on Friday, Governor Kazuo Ueda said underlying inflation had reached 2% but its persistence remained uncertain. He said 2% inflation had not yet become a social norm and described maintaining it for years through appropriate policy adjustment as the remaining task. He offered no specific guidance on the next increase. Bank lending was growing more than 5%, its fastest pace in three decades, which he associated with a reawakening of corporate risk appetite under moderate inflation.

Japan also disclosed a substantial backward-looking portfolio loss. GPIF lost 1.7%, or JPY5.253 trillion, in the quarter through September, its first negative quarter in six. Foreign bonds returned minus 6.52% and domestic bonds minus 1.80%, against a 3.71% gain in Japanese equities and a 1.86% overseas-equity loss. The reporting period included an 81-basis-point increase in 10-year Treasury yields, about 38 basis points in Japanese benchmark yields and a dollar decline of more than 3% against the yen. Assets stood at JPY314.4 trillion.

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi proposed using additional remittances from faster BOJ ETF sales to fund economic-security investments. The BOJ had already announced annual sales of JPY860 billion from January, up from JPY330 billion; Bloomberg Economics estimated the faster pace could increase annual government remittances by about JPY800 billion. Takaichi wants the proceeds directed to a multiyear special account. The government plans initial financing through bridging bonds, whose repayment requires identified future funding sources, making those prospective remittances relevant to the funding proposal.

China's 10-year sovereign yield reached a record intraday low of 1.58%, down about 1 basis point, while the 30-year traded around 2.03%. Haven demand and ample liquidity supported the move. Credit Agricole's Jeffrey Zhang said investors were rebuilding cash-bond positions as earlier credit concerns faded. Standard Chartered's Becky Liu saw limited immediate room for further easing but expected lower, more stable interbank rates to support a modest further yield decline.

In Britain, Huw Pill opened a more conditional path after the previous day's increase to 4%. The BOE chief economist said rates could remain unchanged or fall if growth stalled and the threat of second-round inflation weakened. He described the increase as preemptive and said clearer evidence on wage and price responses to the energy shock would emerge by spring. Governor Andrew Bailey separately said durable progress toward a Middle East settlement could change the policy outlook. Markets in Pill's Friday account assigned about a 60% probability to another increase next month.

Housing data exposed pressure from borrowing costs but also disagreement between measures. Lloyds reported October prices down 0.6% monthly, against expectations of a 0.1% increase, and down 1.2% annually, the largest yearly decline since October 2023. Nationwide instead showed no monthly change and a 0.5% annual increase. France's labor-statistics release added another household strain: private-sector wages fell 1.1% in real terms from a year earlier in Q3.

ECB Chief Economist Philip Lane said Friday that officials were gathering information before December and wanted to contain the energy shock's spread into other prices. In a Saturday-published interview, Lagarde said inflation would remain high in coming quarters and that a change in the expected direction of policy would require significant new information, while declining to commit to a December increase. She said multi-year wage agreements and companies' pay expectations had not shifted beyond the second-round effects already incorporated in projections.

The leadership contest advanced separately: Klaas Knot and Pablo Hernandez de Cos were the only candidates formally nominated before Friday's deadline. De Cos, now head of the BIS, said in a Saturday interview that second-round effects had not yet appeared but persistent energy costs required vigilance. He also warned that high deficits and debt would become more expensive to service as rates rose. His assessment was a candidate's policy view, distinct from the ECB's decision process.

Chile's October CPI provided fresh evidence for its own tightening debate. Annual inflation reached 4.5%, just below the 4.6% forecast, while prices rose 0.5% monthly. Transport increased 2%, energy 2.7% and food and nonalcoholic beverages 1%; clothing fell 4.1%, and inflation excluding food and energy was flat for the month. The release showed a strong supply-cost contribution alongside much quieter underlying monthly prices.

Political disagreement over rate increases also sharpened in the Czech Republic. Prime Minister Andrej Babis attacked Thursday's increase, arguing it would raise household and business borrowing costs and could not influence world energy prices. The central bank's stated concern was the spread of those costs into broader inflation and expectations; Governor Ales Michl maintained that policy would remain independent.

## Restructuring Talks Deteriorate as Sovereign Risks Grow

Braskem's prospective capital support weakened after creditors rejected a proposed $3.8 billion debt-to-equity conversion. People familiar with this week's New York negotiations said Petrobras and IG4 withdrew their proposed injection on the terms then under discussion. The nonbinding proposal had envisaged $1.4 billion of shareholder capital conditional on a debt swap. Talks continued, with parties having until late November to reach an agreement and bankruptcy protection again being considered as an alternative.

Any deal requiring Petrobras support would need its board's approval. Other people familiar with the matter said directors were skeptical of the current terms and would reject them. Braskem said developments would be disclosed through official channels; Petrobras and IG4 did not immediately respond. Its American depositary receipts fell as much as 30% before paring losses. The dispute concerned the terms on which owners would provide new capital after prolonged cash depletion and weak petrochemical prices.

A separate Rhodium Group study published this week for the U.S. Chamber of Commerce described Chinese chemical overcapacity as a threat to overseas producers. Researcher Jeremy Smith linked the problem to capacity expansion followed by the loss of property-related demand after 2021, which pushed more output abroad. He argued that China's efforts to stop price wars and upgrade facilities were unlikely to resolve the pressure on foreign competitors, calling for coordination across value chains. The research added an industry-level explanation for persistent competitive pressure in chemicals.

Brightspeed was discussing $2 billion-$3 billion of fresh capital with creditors as it addressed roughly $10 billion of debt and the costs of its fiber rollout. The amount and whether financing would be arranged inside or outside court remained unsettled, according to people familiar with the talks. The Apollo-backed company had recently warned about its ability to continue as a going concern.

Its securities showed very different recovery expectations within the capital structure. A roughly $2.6 billion delayed-draw term loan was quoted around 66.25 cents Friday, while a roughly $2.5 billion payment-in-kind loan traded near 17.25 cents; both mature in 2031. Fiber sales were up 16% annually, and the company had announced more than 3 million fiber-enabled locations in April. The expansion across 20 states continued to require substantial capital even with that operating growth. A 2024 restructuring had already removed $1.1 billion of debt and supplied $3.7 billion of new capital, while creating different repayment tiers in secured borrowing.

Senegal faced a prospective ratings default tied to its planned debt exchange. Moody's Lucie Villa said the agency would very likely classify the exchange as distressed, even as the country continued making scheduled payments. Senegal was seeking IMF board approval for a $2.2 billion program, and Villa warned that an impasse over the revised 2026 budget could delay approval.

The sovereign's spread stood around 1,469 basis points in JPMorgan's index, and five-year default protection cost 2,145 basis points, more than 33% higher since the debt rework and IMF program were announced September 1. The immediate payment schedule includes $31.25 million of interest on the 2033 securities on November 23 and another $38.75 million due December 10. Moody's assessment concerned the likely treatment of the proposed exchange, alongside those continuing payment obligations.

Argentina's dollar bonds approached distressed spread levels as political uncertainty compounded the global retreat from risk. Its benchmark 2035 yield reached 13.77% Friday from 12.67% at the previous week's end, with the bond losing more than 3 cents. A JPMorgan measure put the sovereign premium at 928 basis points after widening almost 140 basis points over the week's first four days. Argentina's domestic markets were closed Friday for a bank holiday, while its bonds pared some losses in New York.

Pablo Goldberg at BlackRock said investors were anticipating next year's presidential contest earlier than expected. A bond-price model developed by PPI's Pedro Siaba Serrate put Javier Milei's reelection probability around 45%, down from roughly 90% in July. That model-based shift accompanied concern about future access to U.S. backing, including the $20 billion swap line arranged in 2025. Argentina continued to run a fiscal surplus and benefit from strong exports, while investors questioned the durability of political support and the reserve implications of suspected official purchases of local bonds.

Sunday's regional reporting preserved disagreement about Washington's response. Grit Capital's Walter Stoeppelwerth expected Trump to maintain support for Milei. AllianceBernstein's Katrina Butt expected more congressional scrutiny but noted that the swap line had been implemented through executive authority. For Venezuela, she identified increased scrutiny as investors awaited a debt-sustainability analysis initially expected in June, a prerequisite for restructuring tens of billions of dollars of defaulted bonds. In Paraguay, the political crisis advanced to charges against former President Santiago Pena over his alleged role in Ueno Bank's collapse, after the Senate removed him. Those were distinct changes in political and restructuring risk across the region.

## Weekend Energy Developments Complicate Diplomatic Hopes

Oil ended Friday little changed on the day but substantially cheaper over the week. Brent futures rose 0.03% to $98.32 a barrel, leaving a weekly decline of 13.32%, while WTI gained 0.34% to $90.83 and was down 12.76% over the week. Friday reporting said Iran was reviewing a proposal involving its nuclear program and showing willingness to discuss issues previously excluded from negotiations. The diplomatic opening remained conditional as Qatar continued mediation.

The weekend then brought new physical disruption. A drone strike on Iraq's Khor Mor gas field on Sunday hit an LPG storage tank, started a fire and led to suspension of operations. Initial reporting described no deaths and did not establish the perpetrator or the shutdown's duration. The interruption removed about 2.8 gigawatts of electricity-generating capacity from the regional system, a substantial consequence for power supply in Iraqi Kurdistan.

Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein separately said Baghdad had reached understandings with Washington intended to allow Iraqi oil exports through a route close to Oman in the Strait of Hormuz. He estimated losses from disrupted exports at about $60 billion. Iraqi energy officials put October exports near 3.5 million barrels a day, up from 2.65 million in September; that increase preceded Sunday's announcement. Implementation of the newly described transit arrangement remained unresolved.

Maritime-security accounts were less conclusive. Iranian state media described two tankers striking mines and a third vessel catching fire, while U.S. military representatives separately reported commercial-vessel damage during blockade enforcement. Reuters could not independently verify the reported strikes. UKMTO reported a bulk-carrier incident about 18 nautical miles from Khor Fakkan in the UAE, without establishing that the various descriptions concerned the same event. Trump said Sunday that major new U.S. attacks were highly unlikely if a strong agreement could be reached, while also discussing possible infrastructure targets if fighting resumed.

Saudi authorities reported intercepting missiles over Riyadh and eastern Saudi Arabia, with debris damaging windows on several floors of an Aramco administrative building. They described limited damage. The Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi targets, and Saudi authorities reported operations against launch facilities in Yemen. The identified Aramco damage concerned offices; initial reporting established no production, refining or export disruption there. These weekend developments left energy-security conditions unsettled as markets approached reopening.

## Forward Market Significance

October U.S. CPI, scheduled for November 10 at 8:30 a.m. Eastern, is the next major test of the December rate outlook after payroll strength. Consensus expects headline prices to rise 0.3% monthly after 0.6%, and core prices 0.2% after 0.3%. Bloomberg's preview says BLS will not publish year-over-year comparisons because the October 2025 release was skipped during the government shutdown. The decision-useful detail will therefore include the monthly composition of goods, housing and other services, especially after Daly's concern about persistent nonhousing services inflation. Friday's producer-price release is expected to show annual inflation accelerating to 6.6%.

Monday's New York Fed consumer-expectations release will provide a separate household inflation measure after Michigan's decline. Scheduled appearances by Michelle Bowman, Austan Goolsbee and Tom Barkin on November 9, followed by Christopher Waller and Lorie Logan on November 10, offer opportunities to assess how officials reconcile stronger hiring with tighter financial conditions. November employment follows December 4 before the December 9 policy decision.

Treasury's refunding auctions fall around the inflation release and the Veterans Day closure of cash bond trading on Wednesday. Monday's announced $58 billion three-year sale comes first, followed by 10-year notes Tuesday and 30-year bonds Thursday. Friday's rates account indicated the three-year around 4.59%, compared with the previous auction's 4.932% result. The sales will test demand after the rally and partial payroll reversal, without the normal midweek cash session between the latter two auctions.

Corporate funding demand remains substantial. Dealers expect around $40 billion of U.S. high-grade issuance in the coming week. European supply surveys cover different markets: syndicate contacts put a broad corporate total including euro, sterling and offshore dollar deals near EUR13.3 billion-EUR16.1 billion, while a separate high-grade survey found 75% expecting at least EUR30 billion. Anthropic's prospective flotation also faces a valuation reassessment after the technology selloff. The terms on which borrowers secure fresh money remain important alongside the secondary-market recovery in recent euro issues.

Euro-area finance ministers will assess Knot and de Cos on November 9, with the final ECB presidential choice resting with European leaders. The discussion is part of a wider board reshuffle involving the departures of Isabel Schnabel and Philip Lane; leaders' meetings on November 13 and November 26-27 provide subsequent negotiating opportunities. Britain's November 12 GDP release, expected to show 0.7% quarterly growth, will add evidence on the resilience Pill made central to the next policy steps. Japan's forthcoming BOJ opinion summary and household-spending data will help connect strong wages to the durability of domestic demand.

After the U.S. close, policymakers continued to draw distinctions between AI investment's immediate costs and uncertain later benefits. IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva warned that a slowdown in AI-driven growth would alter the environment facing central banks and could create financial-stability risks. On Monday morning in Sydney, RBA economist Sarah Hunter said infrastructure construction was adding demand and cost pressure while aggregate Australian statistics had yet to show meaningful productivity benefits. She described only tentative weakness in job advertising in some AI-exposed occupations. Whether spending slows, financing becomes more selective or productivity improves remains central to how that investment affects inflation and growth.

Energy diplomacy and actual operating conditions retain independent importance. The Khor Mor restart, implementation of Iraq's proposed export routing and the course of U.S.-Iran negotiations will determine whether the weekend brings lasting supply consequences or workable relief. Those developments arrive after a week in which lower inflation compensation supported Treasuries, while Friday's employment news left the near-term case for monetary restraint intact.

overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries retreated Friday after October payrolls rose 165,000 against a 65,000 consensus, earlier gains were revised up by 84,000 and hourly earnings increased 0.4% monthly. The 2-year yield rose 4.92 basis points to 4.5115%, while the 10-year added 2.27 basis points to 4.8574%, flattening the curve. Real yields contributed 1.5 basis points of the 10-year increase and inflation compensation 0.77 basis point. Much of the weekly rally survived: the 10-year yield was still down 7.15 basis points, with lower inflation compensation accounting for that decline as real yields rose over the week.

Mary Daly said labor-market strength gave the Fed room to address persistent inflation. Later Friday swap pricing implied about 20 basis points of December tightening, up from 19 before payrolls. Stronger hiring coexisted with rising underemployment and longer jobless spells, while Michigan's survey showed lower household inflation expectations.

Semiconductors rebounded 4.21%, but the recovery in risk appetite remained selective. U.S. investment-grade and high-yield spreads were little changed, and hard-currency EM spreads tightened modestly. SoftBank's bonds had weakened in earlier Asian trading; recent Meta and Alphabet euro issues benefited from generous issuance terms. Braskem's proposed shareholder support deteriorated after creditors rejected a debt swap, while Brightspeed sought $2 billion-$3 billion of fresh capital. November 10 CPI is the next major test of the December policy outlook.
